_comment: Ratchet config for scripts/codecharta-ratchet.py, run against the CodeCharta map (situs.cc.json.gz). Three gates: (1) per-file aggregate complexity, (2) per-FUNCTION complexity (not gameable by moving code between files), (3) hotspot (complex AND under-tested). Coverage has its own floors in .coverage-floors and mutation its own thresholds in .mutation-thresholds; this gate covers what neither does. Ratchet by LOWERING the numbers as the code improves; RAISING a baseline entry needs a written justification, same rule as the other two ratchets.
_provenance: Baselined 2026-08-21 on feature/codecharta with ccsh 1.143.0, measured — not estimated. Caps and hotspot thresholds are deliberately the same numbers as ortus so the sibling services and the new-go-service template stay uniform; only the baselines are situs' own.

complexity._default_cap_note: Per-file SUM of function complexity. Every file not listed below must stay <= this. Stops a file becoming a monolith, but can be satisfied by splitting a file (the sum moves with the code) — see function_complexity for the non-gameable ceiling. Highest non-baseline file today is 33 (internal/application/localize.go), so there is real headroom before this bites.

baseline._query_note: query.go is the read side's whole use-case layer: five endpoint methods plus IndexInfo and the area/backbone helpers. It is at 100% coverage and 100% mutation efficacy, so the complexity is watched, not unguarded. It said 'split it before letting this number grow', and that is what happened: the German-label overlay pushed it 78 -> 81, the gate refused, and preferredLabel moved to label.go instead of the baseline being raised. 78 -> 73 on the way back. It happened again with the factsheet descriptions: descriptionOf moved to description.go rather than the baseline going up, 73 -> 72. Split it again before letting this grow.
baseline._ingest_note: ingest.go carries one reader per CSV source; each new source adds a block. Also 100% coverage and 100% mutation efficacy. Ratcheted down 64 -> 55 in Task 9 of the syntaxa-quellenumkehr plan: the two syntaxa-hierarchy readers moved to internal/application/syntaxa_ingest.go and syntaxa_parents.go, so this file lost the complexity that came with them.

function_complexity._default_cap_note: The single most complex FUNCTION in a file (McCabe). This is the real overall-complexity control: a function keeps its complexity wherever it lives, so moving it between files cannot game this gate — passing requires actually simplifying the function (or extracting cohesive sub-functions). Note that query.go, ingest.go and localize.go all sit at exactly 10, so any growth in their worst function fails the gate immediately. Repo max today is 12.

baseline._ingest_cmd_note: cmd/situs/ingest.go's runIngest wires the CSV ingest, the localization overlay and the paced distribution source, and reports each phase. The distribution phase must not abort the run on a source outage, which is where the branching comes from.
baseline._paced_distribution_note: cmd/situs/paced_distribution.go's Areas method (moved out of ingest.go in Task 9 of syntaxa-quellenumkehr, unmodified, to bring ingest.go's per-file complexity sum back under the file cap) tolerates per-concept failures instead of aborting the whole distribution batch, and treats a canceled/expired context as the one failure that is NOT tolerated — that branching is where the complexity comes from. Same shape and same measured value (12) as runIngest above; both were already at this level before this task, codecharta was simply not run against them until now (Tasks 7/8 deferred it to Task 9).

hotspot._note: A file is a hotspot when it is complex AND under-tested; new hotspots fail the build. The allowlist is EMPTY on purpose — situs has no file that needs grandfathering, and it should stay that way. The three files above min_complexity (query.go 100%, ingest.go 100%, sqlite/read.go 96.1%) are all far above min_coverage.
